## Phase 2 — fix pushed for review

Both approved mechanism fixes implemented via RED→GREEN TDD; Option 2 (capacity / MCP_RELEASES_CAP / port pool) deferred to 40a7 as instructed.

**Gerrit change:** https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2458 (commit 7ed602339962, `rebar-ticket: 2f46-6871-796f-41c9`, DCO signed, Change-Id I938ec9ab). Awaiting `LLM-Review +1` + `Verified +1`; will NOT close until Verified +1.

**Plan-review gate:** PASS (certified, 0 blocking). Two earlier BLOCKs were resolved by revising the plan before implementing: (G6) Fix 1's drain-first reorder left new-connection intake open, so a landing burst could re-pin the port for the full grace — resolved by adding an explicit intake-stop (`InFlightGauge.begin_draining()` + `MCPRetiringError`) that refuses NEW certified ops during drain; (G1G2) the pre-existing `test_make_sigterm_handler_stops_intake_then_drains` encoded the OLD should_exit-first contract and had to be enumerated as REWRITTEN, not kept green.

**Fix 1 — fast-drain retiring MCP container (`src/rebar/_mcp_health.py`, extracted serving cluster → `src/rebar/_mcp_serving.py`).**
- Added `DEFAULT_UVICORN_GRACEFUL_SECONDS = 10`, threaded as `uvicorn_graceful_seconds` into `run_http_with_grace`'s `uvicorn.Config(timeout_graceful_shutdown=...)`, decoupled from the 1200s certified-op `grace_seconds`.
- Reordered `make_sigterm_handler._on_sigterm`: `gauge.begin_draining()` first (immediate intake-stop), then drain the gauge, then `should_exit` only after gauge==0.
- `InFlightGauge.begin_draining()` + `track()` refusal (`MCPRetiringError`, never increments) so a burst mid-drain is rejected and retries the live container.
- **Invariant preserved & tested:** >0 in-flight ⇒ full `grace_seconds` drain (never cut short); 0 in-flight ⇒ fast drain via the short backstop; new intake refused during drain.
- Module-size: `_mcp_health.py` was at the 800-LOC cap; the shutdown/serving cluster (`drain_then_exit`/`make_sigterm_handler`/`run_http_with_grace`/`run_mcp`) was extracted verbatim along the existing call-graph seam into `_mcp_serving.py` (200 LOC) and re-exported, so importers/tests are unchanged (`_mcp_health.py` now 713 LOC).

RED→GREEN (Fix 1, `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py`): RED first (old should_exit-first ordering / 1200s uvicorn timeout / no intake-stop), then GREEN. Tests: `test_make_sigterm_handler_drains_gauge_before_stopping_intake_2f46` (fast-drain-at-0 + >0-in-flight preservation guard), `test_run_http_with_grace_decouples_uvicorn_grace_from_op_grace_2f46`, `test_gauge_begin_draining_refuses_new_certified_ops_2f46`, `test_make_sigterm_handler_stops_new_intake_immediately_2f46`.

**Fix 3 — mid-redeploy vs wedged before fail-open (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`).**
- Added `bot_unreachable_disposition()`: `redeploying` (docker status restarting/created/removing/paused, or health `starting`) vs `wedged` (running-but-unreachable, unhealthy, no container, or any inspect error → default `wedged`).
- Branched the drain gate's `inflight < 0` case: `redeploying` within `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` ⇒ DEFER (countable `AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED bot-redeploying`, no blind recreate); else (wedged, or bound exhausted) ⇒ existing fail-open (`AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT signal-unavailable` + recreate). Mirrors the 1c0d disposition-contract intent (map the unknown -1 signal onto its own disposition instead of fail-open).

RED→GREEN (Fix 3, `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py`, real-bash harness): mid-redeploy bot DEFERRED (no compose build/up, `AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED bot-redeploying`, deployed-sha unchanged); wedged bot still fails open (`compose build` + `signal-unavailable`); defer is bounded (`DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX=0` falls through).

**Validation:** `make lint` PASS, `make typecheck` PASS (719 files), `test_mcp_http_transport.py` (35) + `test_autodeploy_review_drain.py` (18) + startup-handshake/opcert/tool-offload MCP modules all GREEN (76 pass); 5-mutation check-with-teeth (all killed); module-size scan (all `src/rebar` ≤ 800) + complexity ratchet (new=0 increased=0). Mechanism-1 real-path timing replication confirmed (fast-drain at 0, preserved at >0, burst refused).

**Attribution:** `caused_by` → fd4a-4e91-f179-4932 (origin commit 8297083532a3), recorded as a graph edge and to be signed into the close disposition via `--caused-by`. The mis-dedup `duplicates→6af7` was removed by the orchestrator; `relates_to→40a7` (design-limitation record) stands.
